To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ag(I)-salt is responsible for the rate-limiting C-H activation step of the Pd-cata-lyzed C-H arylation of Cr3(CO)6(C6F5) and related substrates.
phosphine ligated silver carboxylates can carry out C–H activation on electron deficient arenes, and this is the first example of an Ag(I)-mediated C–H activation.
the Ag(I)-carbocylate is responsible in Pd/ Ag-mediated C-H functionalizations and that the rate of the reaction is controlled by the C-H activation rate of this Ag(I)-carboylate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of Ag(I) as a C-H activating agent in the Pd/Ag-catalyzed functionalization of electron-deficient arene substrates.
the role of Ag(I) salts in Pd/ Ag-mediated C-H functionalizations.
the role of the Ag(I)-salt in the Pd/Ag mediated C-H arylation of electron-deficient arene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ag(I) salt is not an oxidant or halide scavenger but a C-H activator in Pd/ Ag-mediated C-H functionalizations.
the Ag(I) salt acts as an efficient C-H activation catalyst in Pd/ Ag-catalyzed reactions.
the Ag(I) salt is not a catalyst, but a stoichiometric additive that is responsible for the rate-determining step in the catalytic cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ag(I) salts can be effective in promoting the C-H activation of electron-deficient arene compounds, and the role of the Ag(I)-carbonylate is not as a halide or oxidant but as the C-H activation reagent.
Ag(I) salts are not simply additives, but are active species in Pd-cocatalyzed C–H activation reactions.
the Ag(I) salt is the catalyst for C-H activation in Pd-cocatalyzed systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in some Pd/Ag mediated C-H functionalization, the Ag(I) additive can be viewed as the catalyst.
the role of Ag(I) salts is much more diverse and complex than what is currently proposed in the literature.
Ag(I)-carbocylates can be used to carry out C-H arylation of electron-deficient arene substrates, without the need for a Pd-catalysts.
